### Round 2: Dinesh

> "He CONCEDED. Four of them. 'I hate that you're not wrong about this.' I'm framing that and hanging it above my desk."

> "You already divided by eight. You didn't forget the filter. You never forget anything. It's exhausting."

> "You found a bug that, at its absolute worst, *doesn't tear*."

> "Two of your findings, one `if`. You're welcome."

Dinesh checked both of Gilfoyle's `te_sync` findings and they hold: the arithmetic is exact. He argued both down to minor, though:

- **One-period gaps.** The bad estimate puts the push at 9.4 ms, still inside the clean window, and the error then fades by an eighth each frame.
- **Spurious edges.** This one needs electrical noise on a push-pull line with pulses only at V-blank, and it costs one or two torn frames before it recovers.

His single fix covers both: once the period is known, accept an edge only if it lands within period/16 of `last_rise + k×period`.

He dismissed the slice-accounting note as something already true before this PR.

Round 3: Gilfoyle is looking at test quality and anything he hasn't covered yet.

  - If the lock is ever wrong, it never comes back. One spurious edge accepted before a period is known, or a real phase step after the panel resets, and from then on every true edge falls outside the window and gets rejected. Today a glitch costs one or two torn frames and then heals. Your fix turns that into rejecting every edge until reboot.
  - `k·period` piles up error. A small error in the period estimate, multiplied by enough missed edges, ends up bigger than period/16. So the longer TE has been flaky, the more likely it is to reject the edge that would have healed it.
  - My dead-TE finding is still open: `period_us` is never cleared. A lock with no way out, sitting on a period that never expires, makes that bug worse. If you add the check, it needs a way to re-acquire, say after N misses in a row: drop the lock, clear the period, start again.

  - The quarter-pixel centroid sweep fails with smoothing off, because steps of 0 or 1 sit outside 0.25±0.07.
  - The depth test compares the smooth result with the non-smooth one, so an inverted comparison inside `ZB_line_aa` gets caught.
  - The opaque-blend tests fail under TinyGL's additive blend.
  - `tearDown` asserts zero net allocation for every test.

This is the "passes for the wrong reason" pattern AGENTS.md warns about.
  - `test_line_width_is_accepted_and_changes_nothing` never draws a line. It draws a triangle, calls `glLineWidth(4)`, then draws a triangle again. If someone made `glLineWidth` widen lines, this test would stay green. Its name claims something it doesn't check.

If the x clip in the patched `ZB_line_aa` plot (`x < 0 || x >= zb->xsize`) is dropped, the write lands in the neighbouring row's pixel, which is in bounds, so ASan is blind and the test passes. Only the y clip is really covered. Reasoned from the code, not mutation-run. Fix: after drawing the left-edge and right-edge vertical lines, assert that the opposite edge column is still black; then mutation-check by removing each of the four guards.
  - [severity:minor] [NEW] [firmware/test/test_glshim/test_glshim.c, test_line_width_is_accepted_and_changes_nothing] Draws only triangles (`draw_triangle_immediately`), never a line, so it cannot detect `glLineWidth` changing line output. Fix: take a reference line with `draw_line`, call `glLineWidth(4)`, redraw it and compare.
  - [severity:minor] [NEW] [firmware/test/test_glshim/test_glshim.c, polygon offset tests] All offset cases use factor and units ≥ 0. The round-1 snap-sign bug (`tinygl_patch.py:248-250`, snap always added positive) is untestable as written. Fix: add a negative-offset case (for example `glPolygonOffset(-1, -1)` on a sloped twin, which should win the tie), and check it fails under the current snap.
  - [severity:minor] [NEW] [tools/tests/test_tinygl_patch.py:135-175] The new tests check that strings are present in the patched source. They pin the text, not the behaviour; the round-1 bias overflow and snap sign both pass them. They're acceptable only alongside behavioural `test_glshim.c` coverage, which has the gaps above.
  - [info] Checked and sound: the centroid-sweep, depth-order (compared against non-smooth), opaque-blend and display-list recompile tests discriminate as claimed; `test_glshim` tearDown enforces zero net allocation per test; `test_hacks.c` fake clock, sync_to_refresh policy test and Unknown Pleasures leak test (64 KB, same as the other GL hacks); `gl_budget.py --override` and the `probe_hacks.py` registry overrides, escaping and non-xlockmore guard are all tested end to end. No files edited, nothing flashed or posted.

The round-1 snap-sign bug (`tinygl_patch.py:248-250`, snap always added positive) is untestable as written. Fix: add a negative-offset case (for example `glPolygonOffset(-1, -1)` on a sloped twin, which should win the tie), and check it fails under the current snap.
  - [severity:minor] [NEW] [tools/tests/test_tinygl_patch.py:135-175] The new tests check that strings are present in the patched source. They pin the text, not the behaviour; the round-1 bias overflow and snap sign both pass them. They're acceptable only alongside behavioural `test_glshim.c` coverage, which has the gaps above.

### Round 3: Gilfoyle

> "So it's not one `if`. It's one `if`, a counter and a reset."

> "9.4 ms inside a window that ends at 9.5 ms is 0.1 ms of margin. That's luck, not a guarantee."

> "I've seen worse from people with a PhD." (This was his grudging verdict on most of `test_glshim.c`.)

He rebutted Dinesh's one-`if` fix: if that phase lock ever locks onto the wrong edge, nothing ever unlocks it, so a glitch that heals today would last until reboot. He then raised four test-quality findings:

- **The canvas-edge smooth-line test.** It asserts only `glshim_is_open()` and relies on AddressSanitizer to catch a bad write. Drop the x clip and the stray pixel lands in the neighbouring row, which is valid memory, so the test still passes.
- **The line-width test.** It never draws a line.
- **No negative polygon offset in any test.** So the snap-sign bug can't fail anything.
- **The patcher tests.** `test_tinygl_patch.py` only checks that strings are present, not what the arithmetic does.

Dinesh is checking those claims now, and may compile a throwaway copy in the scratchpad to test them.

content.text:
## Dinesh vs Gilfoyle Review: Entire trail 37 (PR #69, Unknown Pleasures)

### 3 rounds of mass destruction

Rod, I stopped after round 3 because they'd converged. Dinesh conceded every new point except one, and that one Gilfoyle had already called acceptable. Your working tree is untouched. Dinesh's mutation runs were in a `git archive` export in the scratchpad.

---

### Best of the Banter

**On the patcher:**

> **Gilfoyle:** I came to bury it and it had already filled in its own paperwork. That's the only compliment you get today, Dinesh.
>
> **Dinesh:** I heard that, Gilfoyle. I'm not going to make a thing of it. [pause] I'm making a small thing of it.

**On the delay loop:**

> **Dinesh:** Did you READ the delay loop? … Zero. You reviewed a code path that doesn't execute.
>
> **Gilfoyle:** I hate that you're not wrong about this. Worse, you're right in a way that took me less time to check than it took you to type it.

**On the phase lock:**

> **Dinesh:** Two of your findings, one `if`. You're welcome.
>
> **Gilfoyle:** It's not one `if`. It's one `if`, a counter and a reset.

**On the edge test:**

> **Dinesh:** I ran the mutations. You "reasoned" yours. Write that down. … You were right for the wrong reason.

---

### Verdict

#### Critical (Gilfoyle won, Dinesh conceded)

- **`tools/tinygl_patch.py:150-157`: smooth lines drop alpha.** `ZB_line_aa` reads only r, g and b. The hack's row alpha (`s2`) goes from 0 at the edges up to 1, then settles at 0.5 for the middle rows. On the device every ridge is full white. Fix: carry `v[3]` through and scale `cover` by it under `SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`. You'll need to decide whether you want upstream's look, since you've already approved the current one.
- **`firmware/src/runner/te_sync.c:51-53`: a dead TE line starts waiting again.** Once `since` passes 2³¹ µs, the "edge just landed" clamp fires. The result is 7.4 ms of waiting per frame for 35.8 minutes out of every 71.6. Fix: narrow the clamp to a small negative window, and add tests at `rise + 0x80000000u` and `rise + 0xFFFFFFF0u`.

#### Important (Gilfoyle won after debate)

- **`main.cpp:392-397`: `push=` includes the TE busy-wait.** That breaks what `push=` means in AGENTS.md. The `gl-budget.md` figures survive only because someone subtracted the wait by hand. Fix: a separate `sync=` stat.
- **`te_sync.c:19-30`: the period filter is weak.**
  - A one-period gap is accepted anywhere from 8.0 to 33.0 ms without a closeness check, so a missed edge plus jitter shifts the period by 2 ms. The push then lands with 0.1 ms to spare.
  - A spurious edge 8 to 16.8 ms after a real one keeps the fake edge and rejects the true one, so the comment says the opposite of what happens.
  - Fix: a phase-lock check (within period/16 of `last_rise + k·period`) **plus** a way to unlock it: after N rejections in a row, clear and relock. Add tests for a glitch at +9000 µs and for a half-period phase step.
- **`test_glshim.c:629-639`: the canvas-edge smooth-line test covers only two of its four clip guards.** Dinesh's mutation runs showed that removing `x >= xsize` or `y >= ysize` leaves all 39 tests passing. Fix: draw just inside the right and bottom edges, assert the opposite column or row stays black, and mutation-check all four guards.
- **`tinygl_patch.py:245-255`: polygon offset.**
  - The float-to-`GLint` bias conversion has no clamp, which is undefined behaviour on slivers. Clamp it to ±(1<<29).
  - The snap margin is always positive, so it weakens a negative offset. Give it the offset's sign.
  - Add a negative-offset test, because no current test can catch the snap bug.

#### Contested (Dinesh held his ground)

- **`main.cpp:547` delay-loop `present()`:** it never runs for Unknown Pleasures, because the 10 ms delay is shorter than the 32 ms push. The only leftover is a latent overrun for some future synced hack that asks for a long delay, which deserves a one-line comment.
- **ISR in IRAM calling `gpio_get_level`:** this is safe. Arduino-ESP32 2.0.17 leaves `CONFIG_ARDUINO_ISR_IRAM` unset, so the ISR is held off while the cache is off. Only the claim in `te_sync.h:40` is wrong.
- **`ximage.c`:** it's unreachable for this hack. It still has to link, and 45 vendor hacks use these calls.
- **`resources.c:47-53` class-prefixed lookup:** it's disclosed in the PR body and in commit `18056b2`. ⚠️ It does change a lookup every xlockmore hack goes through, so AGENTS.md needs your explicit OK. Both sides left that to you.
- **`test_tinygl_patch.py:135-175` string tests:** these check that each patch lands. The behaviour itself is pinned by the C tests.

#### Dismissed (Gilfoyle was nitpicking)

- The two volatile loads in `te_sync.h`: harmless, since the ISR and loop share a core.
- The extra `startWrite` under `TE_DIAG`: it only exists in the diagnostic build.
- The `probe_hacks.py` `REGISTRY_HEAD` duplication and the triple `build_src_filter` in `platformio.ini`: both were already on `main`. A reasonable chore for another day.
- The `list[str] = ()` annotation: a typing nit.

### Strengths

- The patcher checks every anchor count exactly and pins `memory.c` by SHA-256, so no patch can silently do nothing.
- Most of `test_glshim.c` really does pin behaviour:
  - the centroid sweep fails with smoothing off
  - depth order is compared against the non-smooth result
  - the opaque-blend tests fail under additive blend
  - `tearDown` asserts zero net allocation for every test
- The `easing.c` and `doubletime.c` shims match upstream.
- The opaque-fill patch affects only Unknown Pleasures and is documented.
- `gl_budget.py --override` is tested end to end.
- The hack copy is byte-identical: I checked it with `cmp`.

### Score

**Gilfoyle 13 | Dinesh 9.** Dinesh's best moment was running real mutations against Gilfoyle's reasoned claim and partly refuting it.

### Recommended Changes

- [ ] `tools/tinygl_patch.py` `ZB_line_aa`: carry vertex alpha through and scale coverage by it (or decide to keep the current look and document it in `gl.md`)
- [ ] `firmware/src/runner/te_sync.c:51-53`: narrow the negative-`since` clamp; add the long-gap tests
- [ ] `firmware/src/runner/te_sync.c:19-30`: phase-lock acceptance with an unlock after N rejections; add tests for a glitch at +9000 µs, a gap of 2·period−700 and a half-period step
- [ ] `firmware/src/main.cpp:392-397`: time the sync wait as its own `sync=` stat, outside `push=`
- [ ] `tools/tinygl_patch.py:245-255`: clamp the bias and give the snap margin the offset's sign
- [ ] `test_glshim.c`:
  - right and bottom edge assertions, then mutation-check all four guards
  - a real line in the line-width test
  - a negative polygon-offset test
- [ ] `te_sync.h:40`: correct the "uses nothing in flash" comment
- [ ] `registry.c:89-94`: fix the stale 30 ms delay comment
- [ ] `.claude/rules/device-display.md:99`: say "film rows"
- [ ] The `sync_to_refresh` comment: note the latent delay overrun
- [ ] **You:** confirm the shared-lookup change in `resources.c`

None of this has been posted to the trail or the PR.

*Want a comic strip of the best moments? (y/N/pr)*

On the device every ridge draws at full intensity. Fix: carry the vertex colour's v[3] into the line path and scale cover by it under SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, or document the divergence in .claude/rules/gl.md.     ("dg37-te-wrap", "high", "firmware/src/runner/te_sync.c", 51, 53,
     "Dead-TE timeout comes back after 2^31 us. period_us is only cleared by an edge, so once now - last_rise_us passes 2^31 the (int32_t)since < 0 clamp sets since = 0 and every frame waits offset_us (7.4 ms) for about 35.8 minutes in every 71.6.     ("dg37-te-phase-lock", "medium", "firmware/src/runner/te_sync.c", 18, 36,
     "Once the period is known, two gaps in the edge filter: (1) the single-period branch (line 22) accepts any gap from 8,000 to 33,000 us with no closeness check, and 33,000 is only 0.64 ms below two periods (33,638), so a missed edge plus 0.7 ms jitter moves the estimate +2,014 us to 18,833 and the push lands at about 9.4 ms after the rise, 0.1 ms inside the filmed clean window; (2) a spurious rising edge 8-16.8 ms after a real one passes line 19 and becomes last_rise_us, and the next true edge (under 8 ms later) is then rejected as 'a glitch: keep the true edge', the reverse of the comment, giving 1-2 frames pushed at about 16.4 ms (seam band).     ("dg37-film-rows", "low", ".claude/rules/device-display.md", 99, 99,

]

### Update: `./AGENTS.md` (Rules, the test bullet near line 122)

```diff
+  AddressSanitizer sees only writes past either end of a buffer: an x
+  overflow on an inner canvas row wraps into the next row unseen, so a clip
+  test must assert pixels, not just survive (`test_glshim`'s edge test missed
+  the right and bottom guards).
```

### Update: `./AGENTS.md` (Commands)

**Why:** this session reviewed and mutation-checked another branch without touching the checkout on `main`.

```diff
+  `git archive` export in the scratchpad, with `vendor/` symlinked.
```

Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/.claude/skills/markdown

# GitHub Flavored Markdown Generation

**Version:** 1.2.1

Generate GFM that passes markdownlint validation with zero violations.

## Core Principles

### 1. Blank Lines Are Mandatory

- Before/after ALL lists (MD032)
- Before/after ALL headings except document start (MD022)
- Before/after ALL code blocks (MD031)
- Between ALL block-level elements

### 2. Consistency Required

- Use `-` for lists
- Use `#` for headings (ATX)
- Regular spaces only—never tabs/nbsp

### 3. Structure Matters

- Heading hierarchy: 1→2→3 (not 1→3)
- ONE H1 per document
- Files end with one newline
- Lines under 80 chars

### 4. Invisible Characters Matter

- Use ONLY regular spaces (U+0020)
- Never non-breaking spaces (U+00A0,  )
- Never tabs
- UTF-8 encoding

## Pre-Generation Checklist

- [ ] Where will lists/headings/code appear?
- [ ] Heading levels verified (1→2→3)?
- [ ] Using `-` for all lists?
- [ ] Code languages specified?
- [ ] Lines under 80 chars?
- [ ] Line breaks needed? (two trailing spaces)
- [ ] Using regular spaces only?
- [ ] URLs wrapped in `<>` or `[]`?
- [ ] Document starts with H1?
- [ ] Ordered lists use `1.` for all items?
- [ ] File ends with single newline?
- [ ] Tables use consistent spacing?

## Essential Rules

### Lists (MD032, MD004)

```markdown
Text before.

- Item one
- Item two

Text after.
```

### Headings (MD001, MD022)

```markdown
Text.

## Heading

Content.
```

### Code Blocks (MD031, MD040)

````markdown
Text.

```python
code()
```

Text.
````

**Nested Fences:** When showing markdown examples that contain code blocks,
use **one more backtick** than the deepest level:

- Three backticks (` ``` `): Regular code
- Four backticks (` ```` `): Markdown examples with code
- Five backticks (` ````` `): Nested markdown examples

`````markdown
````markdown
# Example

```bash
command
```

````
`````

### Line Length (MD013)

Break long lines at natural points. Use reference-style links for long URLs.

### URLs and Email (MD034)

Wrap bare URLs and emails:

```markdown
Wrong: https://example.com
Right: <https://example.com>
Right: [link](https://example.com)

Wrong: user@example.com
Right: <user@example.com>
```

### Document Structure (MD041)

Start with H1 (or front matter then H1):

```markdown
# Document Title

First paragraph.
```

### Ordered Lists (MD029)

Use `1.` for all items:

```markdown
1. First
1. Second
1. Third
```

### File Endings (MD047)

End with single newline:

```text
Last content line.
[single newline]
[EOF]
```

### Table Column Style (MD060)

Use consistent spacing in tables. Three styles:

**Compact (recommended):** `| cell |` - single space around content

```markdown
| Header 1 | Header 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Data | More data |
```

**Aligned:** Pipes vertically aligned with padding

**Tight:** `|cell|` - no spaces

Pick ONE style per document. Compact is preferred.

### Character Encoding

**Detection:** View → Render Whitespace in VS Code

**Fix:** Find `\u00A0` → Replace with space

**Critical for AI:** Two trailing spaces = intentional line breaks. Do NOT
remove them.

## Critical Error Patterns

### 1. List Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD032 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text:
- Item
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD032 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text:

- Item

Text.
```

### 2. Heading Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD022 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text.
## Head
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD022 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text.

## Head

Text.
```

### 3. Code Without Blanks/Language

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD031 MD040 -->

**Wrong:**

````markdown
Text:
```
code
```
Text.
````

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD031 MD040 -->

**Right:**

````markdown
Text:

```python
code
```

Text.
````

### 4. Inconsistent Markers

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD004 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
- Item
* Item
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD004 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
- Item
- Item
```

### 5. Skipping Levels

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD001 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
# Title

### Sub (skipped H2)
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD001 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
# Title

## Section

### Sub
```

## Post-Generation Validation

1. Lists have blank lines before/after
2. Headings have blank lines before/after
3. Code has blank lines before/after
4. Heading progression: 1→2→3→4
5. All lists use `-`
6. All code has language
7. Lines under 80 chars
8. Document starts with H1
9. URLs wrapped properly
10. Ordered lists use `1.`
11. File ends with one newline
12. Two trailing spaces used intentionally
13. Only regular spaces (no nbsp/tabs)
14. Tables use consistent column spacing

## Mental Model

Markdown is **blocks with mandatory spacing:**

```text
[Text Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Heading Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[List Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Code Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Text Block]
[EOF]
```

Every block transition = blank line required.

## Quick Patterns

**List:**

```markdown
text

- item

text
```

**Heading:**

```markdown
text

## Head

text
```

**Code:**

````markdown
text

```lang
code
```

text
````

**Nested:**

```markdown
- parent
  - child
- parent
```

**Ordered:**

```markdown
text

1. item
1. item

text
```

**Table:**

```markdown
text

| Header | Header |
| --- | --- |
| Cell | Cell |

text
```

## Common Languages

**Programming:** `python` `javascript` `java` `c` `cpp` `go` `rust` `ruby`
`php` `swift` `kotlin` `typescript`

**Shell:** `bash` `sh` `powershell` `cmd` `zsh`

**Markup:** `html` `css` `xml` `json` `yaml` `toml` `markdown`

**Database:** `sql` `postgresql` `mysql`

**Other:** `text` `diff` `log`

## Validation

```bash
markdownlint filename.md
```

Goal: Zero errors/warnings.

## Additional Resources

See bundled references:

- `references/complete-rules.md` - Full rule catalog
- `references/edge-cases.md` - Platform quirks
- `references/examples.md` - Detailed examples

## Remember

---
name: deliver-branch
description: Use when opening, updating, rebasing, merging or cleaning up a branch or PR in this repo: entire trail create, PR body sync, findings, stacked PRs, rebase conflicts, deleting a merged branch.
---

# Delivering a branch

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

- `entire trail create --title ... --type feature --body ...` pushes the branch
  (`--type` takes only `bug`, `feature` or `task`; `chore` is refused)
  and opens a linked DRAFT PR. The PR body is not synced from the trail: update
  both (`entire trail update --body`, `gh pr edit N --body-file`). Put
  `Fixes #N` in the body, then read the PR back (`gh pr view N --json body`):
  #27 merged with the generic body, so `Fixes #23` never reached GitHub and
  the issue stayed open until it was closed by hand.
- Rod approves and merges (merge commit). Afterwards delete the merged branch
  (remote and local) without asking and fast-forward `main`. Confirm the merge
  after a fresh `git fetch`: a stale `origin/main` says "not merged". Remove
  the branch's worktree first (a checked-out branch cannot be deleted), and
  note that `git branch -d` refuses while local `main` is behind, so check
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> origin/main` and then use `-D`. `main` is
  usually checked out in Rod's main checkout, so `git fetch origin main:main`
  is refused there: run `git merge --ff-only origin/main` in it, only if
  `git status` shows no tracked changes.
- Merge with `gh pr ready N` then `gh pr merge N --merge` once Rod approves
  (trail PRs are drafts). His approval is enough: do not wait for the Entire
  Gates check to finish. A stacked PR's gate
  can fail "Up to date: 1 commit behind" once its parent merges: if approvals
  and findings pass and the PR is mergeable, merge it, with no rebase.
- `entire agent-help` says trails are unavailable; `entire trail create` works.
  Write a PR body to a file for `gh pr edit --body-file` (an apostrophe in an
  inline `--body '...'` must be `'"'"'`).
- `gh pr edit N --body-file` replaces the whole body, including the
  `<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->` ... `-end -->` block at the top. Keep that
  block in the file, or the PR loses its trail.
- Findings: `entire trail finding list N`, then `... resolve N <id> -m "..."`.
  Bot reviews can lag about 20 minutes. `N` is the trail number (PR #12 was
  trail 6), not the PR number. For a false positive or upstream behaviour in a
  byte-identical hack, use `entire trail finding dismiss N <id> -m "<reason>"`.
- In a worktree session create the trail with a one-line `--body`, then set the
  real body with `gh pr edit N --body-file` (keep the trail-link block), and
  check `closingIssuesReferences` with `gh pr view N --json` (it can lag a
  few seconds).
- `entire trail update --body` takes no number and acts on the current
  branch (`entire trail update 8` errors).
- Stacked PR: `entire trail create --base <parent-branch>`. When the parent
  merges, `gh pr edit N --base main` before deleting its branch, then
  `git rebase --onto origin/main <old parent tip>`. The rebased push needs
  `--force-with-lease` (ask Rod first), unless the branch was never pushed.
- `docs/porting-assessment.md` conflicts on rebase: `git checkout --theirs`
  it to continue, then rerun `tools/score_hacks.py` and amend the result in.
- Two ports in flight both append to `g_hacks[]`, so whichever merges second
  conflicts in `registry.c`, the expected list in `test_hacks.c`,
  `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `tools/assessment_measured.md` (rows, paragraphs and
  the hack count) and the three `build_src_filter` lines in `platformio.ini`,
  as well as the generated assessment. Keep both sides, put the newer hack
  last, and regenerate the assessment. A rebased published branch needs
  `--force-with-lease` (ask Rod), and GitHub can reject that push once too.
- A finding that says the code "does not exist" can be stale after a rebase
  (the skill PR was reviewed before the Blaster and Substrate code it referred
  to had landed). Check it against `main` before dismissing, and put the
  evidence in the dismissal. Entire's approvals gate once showed "no reviewers
  have approved" right after a force push, though Rod had approved; his word is
  enough, so say so and go ahead.
